name: The Jazz Butcher
label: Creation
lede: Pat Fish started the Jazz Butcher as a one-night joke at his Oxford college in 1982, then kept it going through a fistfight with his co-founder, a Bauhaus rhythm section and the Oasis years at Creation, until his death in 2021.

eras.title: A one-off laugh at Merton College
eras.text: Pat Fish, born Patrick Huntrods, read classics at Merton College, Oxford, and had already played with Max Eider in the Institution and the Sonic Tonix. The Jazz Butcher was meant to last one night. Fish's home tapes got it a record deal instead.

years.cap: The Jazz Butcher at the Black Lion, Northampton, December 1982
years.src: Wikipedia: The Jazz Butcher · Wikipedia: Pat Fish
years.h: The first Jazz Butcher gig is at Merton College
years.p: Fish and Eider play the first advertised show under the name in Oxford. Fish said the name and the gig were "perceived as a one-off laugh."

years.h: An Amstrad cassette deck wins over Glass Records
years.p: Fish built his demos by bouncing parts through an Amstrad 7090's mic channel. Glass founder David Barker heard them and booked Starforce Studio in Clapham.
years.xp: Barker co-produced the sessions under the name Lionel Brando. Eider, Rolo McGinty, Alice Thompson and others played on them.

years.cap: The Jazz Butcher at the Derngate Centre, Northampton, September 1983
years.h: In Bath of Bacon: a few mates and an LP
years.p: The debut on Glass. Fish called it the sound of friends "failing to take seriously the fact they they've got an LP to make."

years.h: John Peel plays 'Southern Mark Smith'
years.p: The Glass single gets the band national attention through [[John Peel|e4dec348-ad10-43b6-a2b1-c22aab890675]]'s radio show. That summer [[Kevin Haskins|476cc87e-9665-43bb-80ea-7e123390ac64]] of [[Bauhaus|0688add2-c282-4ee2-ba61-223ffdb3c201]] joins on drums.

eras.title: Bauhaus in the engine room
eras.text: With two members of Bauhaus behind him, Fish made his best-selling records for Glass and toured hard. By the end of 1986 the touring had worn everyone down, and the partnership with Eider ended in a Swiss dressing room.

years.h: David J joins, and Eider's 'D.R.I.N.K.' backs a Richman cover
years.p: [[David J|41225e9f-3b4c-4287-a778-165c65f04be9]] joins his [[Bauhaus|0688add2-c282-4ee2-ba61-223ffdb3c201]] bandmate Haskins in the rhythm section. The [[Jonathan Richman|bae34b81-9abd-416e-a720-fedc359df775]] cover 'Roadrunner' reaches No. 50 on the indie chart, and Eider's B-side becomes a fan favourite.

years.cap: Live at Onkel Po, Hamburg, December 1984
years.h: A Scandal in Bohemia sells over 20,000
years.p: Produced by John A. Rivers with a sleeve by comic artist Hunt Emerson. Fish: "We were young(ish) and cocky and I think it shows."

years.h: David J leaves to start Love and Rockets
years.p: He and Haskins go on to form [[Love and Rockets|8cb3aa4a-3b4c-48b8-be0a-e57010fc1430]]. Graham "Felix" Fudger, known as Felix Ray, takes the bass.

years.cap: Live at the Loft, Berlin, November 1985
years.h: 110 shows, and Fish's favourite Glass album
years.p: The band plays 110 shows in 1985, up from 36 the year before. Sex and Travel, again with Rivers, was the Glass record Fish liked best.
years.xp: The same year brought a live album, Hamburg, credited to The Jazz Butcher and His Sikkorskis from Hell, plus the singles 'Real Men' and 'The Human Jungle'.

years.cap: Live at the Warehouse, Leeds, October 1986
years.h: Rivers goes digital on Distressed Gentlefolk
years.p: Producer John A. Rivers puts his new digital gear all over the fourth album. 'Hard' reaches No. 24 on the indie chart.

years.h: Fish and Eider come to blows after a Zurich show
years.p: Tension, drink and exhaustion end in a physical fight, and Eider quits. It's nine years before the two play together again.

eras.title: McGee keeps the name
eras.text: The Glass deal ran out after a compilation, and Alan McGee was waiting. On Creation Records the Butcher became a loose, rotating group: borrowed Weather Prophets, Spacemen 3's Sonic Boom, saxophone, and five albums in five years.

years.big: "That's the one they all know, you've got to keep it."
q: That's the one they all know, you've got to keep it.
years.h: Alan McGee comes to a Paris duo show with a Creation offer
years.p: Fish and saxophonist Alex Green are playing as a duo. McGee wants him on Creation and won't let him drop the Jazz Butcher name.
years.xp:
McGee called Fish "one of the most brilliant incisive pop writers that Britain has produced since the glory days of Ray Davies and Pete Townshend."

The new band: Kizzy O'Callahan on guitar, Dave Goulding and Dave Morgan borrowed from [[The Weather Prophets|8bd0e8b7-081a-4b32-b855-b38134074b35]], and Green on sax, with Sonic Boom of [[Spacemen 3|19e818e4-0bbe-41fc-9589-c444b4165bf1]] and members of [[The Perfect Disaster|6d7e05e9-3090-4e79-8747-6a6ad621cf92]] sitting in.

years.cap: The Jazz Butcher at the Market Tavern, London, September 1988
years.h: Fish poses in a chip shop called Fishcotheque
years.p: Mitch Jenkins shoots Fish and new guitarist Kizzy O'Callahan inside the London fish-and-chip shop for the first Creation album's cover. The Classics IV cover 'Spooky' reaches No. 19 on the indie chart.

years.cap: Pat Fish at Shank Hall, Milwaukee, November 1989
years.src: Wikipedia: The Jazz Butcher · Wikipedia: Pat Fish
years.h: Hip-hop and proto-acid on Big Planet Scarey Planet
years.p: Fish named both as influences. 'Line of Death' mixes Middle Eastern melody, disco, heavy metal and Ennio Morricone.
years.xp:
Rivers produced again. Pascal Legras did the cover and went on to draw most of the band's 1990s artwork. Drummer Paul Mulreany had joined the live band.

Fish also spent 1989 presenting the indie music TV show Transmission.

years.h: O'Callahan's brain tumour, days before a nine-week US tour
years.p: Guitarist Kizzy O'Callahan is taken to hospital and diagnosed. [[Richard Formby|df65e89f-537a-4b26-ae31-f2923755fb0e]] takes his place for the tour. In LA the band records a session for KCRW's SNAP! on December 6.

years.cap: Pat Fish at the Paradise, Boston, November 1990
years.h: Fish hears his real band on Cult of the Basement
years.p: Fish: "I feel it's the first time we captured the true sound of the band." The video for 'Girl Go' plays on MTV's 120 Minutes.
years.xp:
'Girl Go' and 'Mr. Odd' were broken in on the road. The B-side 'Excellent' was O'Callahan's last appearance with the band; he died of the brain tumour in 1993.

Fish's ambient dance side project Black Eg, credited to the fictional Von Dämmerung brothers, followed on Creation in 1991.

years.h: Fish's marriage ends and Condition Blue comes out of it
years.p: His marriage fell apart during a tour with The Blue Aeroplanes, and the album goes to darker places. Fish stayed proud of it as "writing about a tough subject."
years.xp:
Fish had married Barbara J. Taylor in a small Northamptonshire ceremony in 1987; they divorced.

He disliked the US version's running order: "It makes no sense at all." Mulreany, Alex Lee and Joe Allen were the core band, with Formby, Green, Owen Jones and Peter Astor contributing.

eras.title: Oasis business
eras.text: Creation's world shrank to one band from Manchester. Fish made Illuminate, tried techno as Sumosonic, got a letter from McGee, and by spring 1998 he was off the label.

years.h: David J comes back to produce Illuminate
years.p: Punk shots at the Tory government, songs about dolphins, tributes to [[Brian Eno|ff95eb47-41c4-4f7f-a104-cdc30f02e872]] and Hammer Films, and a utopia run by dinosaurs.
years.xp: Creation was about to change. McGee had sold half the company to Sony, and [[Oasis|39ab1aed-75e0-4140-bd47-540276886b60]]'s (What's the Story) Morning Glory? was coming. Fish: "Honestly, there wasn't enough time in the day to do anything other than handle Oasis business."

years.h: Eider and Fish play 'Zombie Love' together again
years.p: Eider opens a London show and the two share the stage for the first time since Zurich in 1986.

years.big: "We'd better jack it in before you get bitter."
q: We'd better jack it in before you get bitter.
years.h: McGee lets Fish go by letter
years.p: The Sumosonic techno album This Is Sumo sells poorly, and Fish is off Creation by March. The label itself shuts in 1999.

years.cap: The reunited band at Sy Klopps Studios, San Francisco, September 1999
years.h: The original line-up reunites at the Troubadour in LA
years.p: Fish, Eider, [[Owen Jones|77673613-772d-426e-9a9a-cc6b07f00191]], David J and Haskins play together for the first time since 1985. Fish, Eider and Jones tour the US in 2000 behind Rotten Soul.

eras.title: Live from Fishy Mansions
eras.text: Fans paid for a 30th-anniversary album, Fire Records bought the catalogue, and in the pandemic Fish played to the world from his living room in Northampton.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Jazz Butcher · Fire Records
years.h: A crowdfunding target hit by bedtime
years.p: Fish and Eider's PledgeMusic campaign is at about 120 percent the first night. Alan Moore writes the liner notes.
years.xp:
Recorded in August and September 2012 at Formby's studio in Leeds, with Sonic Boom and Owen Jones. The first 500 copies sold out, another 500 were pressed, and Fire Records took on the album and the whole back catalogue.

Fire boxed the four Glass albums as The Wasted Years in 2017 and four Creation albums as The Violent Years in 2018.

years.cap: A Fishy Mansions livestream, Northampton, December 2020
years.h: Fish plays requests from his living room
years.p: With gigs stopped by COVID-19, the "Live From Fishy Mansions" streams draw hundreds of viewers, old bandmates among them. Fish had been treated for cancer since November 2018 and got his remission letter in June.

years.cap: Fish with Joe Woolley at the Continental, Preston, August 2021
years.src: Wikipedia: The Jazz Butcher · Wikipedia: Pat Fish
years.h: Pat Fish dies of a heart attack at home in Northampton
years.p: He was 63, and had cancelled a Fishy Mansions show two days earlier, citing exhaustion. A November gig at the Dublin Castle in London became a tribute night.

years.h: The Highest in the Land arrives four months after Fish's death
years.p: Recorded June 26, 2021 with Eider, Dave Morgan, Tim Harries and Peter Crouch, released on Tapete.

years.h: Max Eider, co-founder, dies
years.p: Brooklyn Vegan reported the death of the guitarist who played the first gig at Merton in 1982.
